transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
I’m here because when I eat too much, I make myself throw up afterward so I won’t gain weight. It’s gotten to the point where I’m scared I can’t stop doing it.
Before you make yourself throw up, do you usually eat an unusually large amount of food in a short period of time?

Yes. Usually late at night, after everyone’s quiet, I’ll just stand in the kitchen eating whatever’s there—leftovers, cereal, chips, ice cream. It goes way past a normal meal. By the end, it feels like half the pantry has been picked over.
During those times when you eat that much, do you feel like you can’t stop or control what you’re eating?
Yes. Once I start, it feels like my hands just keep grabbing food even while I’m telling myself, Lucy, knock it off. I don’t feel in control again until it’s already over.
How much does your body shape or weight affect how you feel about yourself as a person?

A lot. If my work pants feel tight, or I catch sight of my belly in the mirror, I just feel like I’m failing at everything. Like I’m not the strong woman I used to be—the one who could handle transmissions and keep up with the guys.
How often do these binge-and-vomit episodes happen?
For at least the last three months, hardly a week goes by without it happening at least once. Some weeks it’s several times, especially when I’m home more because of my back.
